run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T05:36:00Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a brief outage on the checkout path, not by a fault in frontend-proxy itself. At 2026-11-15T05:36:13Z the single-replica payment Deployment was restarted (pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-15T05:36:13Z; new ReplicaSet payment-79d86bf97f scaled 0->1, old ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 scaled 1->0, old pod payment-55766d76b9-5frt4 deleted at 05:36:18Z). The replacement container started at 05:36:17Z but its gRPC server only logged "payment gRPC server started on port 8080" at 05:37:34.791Z, and the payment container spec carries no readiness/startup probe, so the Service had no serving payment backend for roughly 1-2 minutes. Checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge client spans then failed: the checkout Charge STATUS_CODE_ERROR counter went 0 (05:36:00Z) -> 41 (05:37) -> 80 (05:38) -> 81 (05:39) and stayed 81, while successful (UNSET) Charge calls stalled at 1079 across the 05:37/05:38/05:39 samples. Failures propagated as 81 failed checkout PlaceOrder server spans, 81 failed frontend POST /api/checkout + PlaceOrder client spans and +81 frontend-proxy "router frontend egress" / +85 "ingress" error spans between 05:36:00Z and 05:45:00Z, producing the frontend-proxy request-error spike that triggered the alert. Errors attributed to payment stopped after ~05:39-05:44 (counters flat through the end of metric data at 05:51:00Z), and payment processed charges normally afterwards ("Transaction complete." for each "Charge request received." from 05:41Z onwards).

claims.text: frontend-proxy emits span metrics only for two operations: SERVER "ingress" and CLIENT "router frontend egress", and both have STATUS_CODE_ERROR series present in the incident window (in addition to STATUS_CODE_UNSET).

Over the full 04:36:00Z-05:59:17Z window, frontend-proxy accumulated 96.64 errored "ingress" spans and 82.40 errored "router frontend egress" spans (increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total with status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR), against 23,418.93 and 23,431.14 UNSET spans respectively.

The frontend-proxy error counters rose mainly between 05:36:00Z and 05:45:00Z: ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR 499 -> 584 (+85) and "router frontend egress" STATUS_CODE_ERROR 467 -> 548 (+81); they then stayed essentially flat through 05:51:00Z (ingress 587, egress 548).

The per-service error rate peaked at the 05:39:00Z evaluation point: frontend 5.2 errored spans/s, checkout 2.6/s, frontend-proxy 2.4667/s (rate over 60s), while payment was 0/s in that same query; before 05:36Z and after 05:41Z frontend-proxy's error rate was in the 0-0.13 spans/s range.

The errored spans are the checkout path: frontend CLIENT "grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder", INTERNAL "executing api route (pages) /api/checkout", SERVER "POST" and SERVER "POST /api/checkout"; checkout CLIENT "oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge" and SERVER "oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder". Raw errored-span counters moved from 72/72/72/72/0/0 at 05:36:00Z to 153/153/166/153/81/81 at 05:45:00Z (frontend), and frontend's POST /api/checkout error counter was still 153 at 05:51:00Z.

Checkout's Charge calls failed while successful calls stalled: checkout "oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge" STATUS_CODE_ERROR was 0 at 05:36:00Z, 41 at 05:37:00Z, 80 at 05:38:00Z and 81 from 05:39:00Z onward, and the UNSET (successful) Charge counter stayed at 1079 across the 05:37/05:38/05:39 samples before rising to 1111 by 05:40:00Z and 1478 by 05:50:00Z.

The payment Deployment was restarted at 05:36:13Z: its pod template carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-15T05:36:13Z, Deployment events at 05:36:13Z show "Scaled up replica set payment-79d86bf97f from 0 to 1" and "Scaled down replica set payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0" (the down-scale event is timestamped 05:36:18Z), and pod payment-55766d76b9-5frt4 was "Killing"/SuccessfulDelete at 05:36:18Z while payment-79d86bf97f-9pm9t was Scheduled 05:36:13Z and its container Started 05:36:17Z.

The new payment container (payment-79d86bf97f-9pm9t) logged "payment gRPC server started on port 8080" only at 2026-11-15T05:37:34.791Z, its first "Charge request received." at 05:38:21.991Z, and "14 UNAVAILABLE: Connection dropped" at 05:38:30.851Z - i.e. the gRPC listener came up about 78s after the container Started event (05:36:17Z) and about 77s after the old pod was deleted (05:36:18Z).

The old and new payment ReplicaSet pod templates are otherwise identical: image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, same env (PAYMENT_PORT=8080, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, OTEL_* values), same resources (limits cpu 20m / memory 160Mi) and same labels; only the restartedAt annotation differs, and the container spec in both templates has no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe. The Deployment uses RollingUpdate with maxSurge 25% and maxUnavailable 25% on 1 replica.

No other workload change or failure event occurred in otel-demo during the incident: the only events since 05:20:00Z are the 9 payment rollout events (Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started/SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete/Killing/ScalingReplicaSet), and all 21 pods are Running with ready=true and restartCount 0 except flagd's two containers at 0; the only pod started inside the incident window is payment-79d86bf97f-9pm9t at 05:36:13Z (others started 05:04-05:06Z, frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-b9w85 at 05:04:17Z).

After the burst the checkout Charge error counter stayed at 81 through 05:51:00Z and payment processed charges normally: its log lines from 05:41:21Z to 05:47:09Z pair every "Charge request received." with "Transaction complete." (and the pod/Deployment show 1/1 ready, available, updated).

A small steady error signal predates and outlives the burst: frontend-proxy error rates of 0.0037-0.0111 errored spans/s appear at 05:17-05:35Z and again at 05:47-05:51Z, and frontend's cumulative error counters for "GET", "GET /api/data", "grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds" and "executing api route (pages) /api/data" were 385/379/379/379 at both 05:36:00Z and 05:45:00Z (no increase); those series did not appear in a whole-window increase query filtered to >0, while the checkout-path series did.

Payment's own server spans did not report the failures: payment "grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge" STATUS_CODE_ERROR was 0 for the whole window until a single error appeared at the 05:41:00Z sample (1), while 1182 such spans were recorded as STATUS_CODE_UNSET; the 60s-rate error query showed payment at 0/s during the burst. This argues that the failed Charge calls failed in transport/at the client rather than payment returning application errors.

Primary cause: restarting the single-replica payment Deployment at 05:36:13Z (kubectl rollout restart annotation) removed the only serving payment pod (deleted 05:36:18Z) while the replacement's gRPC server did not start listening until 05:37:34.791Z; because the payment container has no readiness/startup probe, the new pod was treated as Ready as soon as its container started (05:36:17Z) and received Service traffic before it could serve. Checkout's PaymentService/Charge calls therefore failed (81 errored client spans, with the payment side logging "14 UNAVAILABLE: Connection dropped"), which made checkout PlaceOrder and frontend /api/checkout fail and raised frontend-proxy's request error rate above zero, triggering RequestErrorRate for otel-demo/frontend-proxy.

Secondary candidate for why the alert remained in an "above 0" state after the payment-related burst ended: frontend-proxy continues to record a small number of errors on its own operations (ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR 584 at 05:45:00Z -> 587 at 05:51:00Z, and error rates of 0.0037-0.0118 errored spans/s in 05:17-05:35Z and 05:47-05:51Z). Which operation or downstream produces these residual errors is not established by the available evidence.

Rejected: an application defect in the payment service's Charge handler. During the failure interval the payment server had not yet started its gRPC listener (start log 05:37:34.791Z, first Charge received 05:38:21.991Z), once serving it logged "Transaction complete." for every charge, it recorded essentially no error spans, its container restart count is 0, and the only error text is the transport-level "14 UNAVAILABLE: Connection dropped".

Rejected: resource pressure, eviction or a crash on the payment pod. No Evicted, OOMKilling, Unhealthy/BackOff or Failed events exist in otel-demo since 05:20:00Z (only the 9 payment rollout events), the payment pod's restartCount is 0 and its phase is Running with ready=true.

Rejected: frontend-proxy itself was restarted, reconfigured or crashed at the alert time. Its pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-b9w85 started 05:04:17Z with restartCount 0, phase Running, ready=true, and no event in otel-demo since 05:20:00Z involves frontend-proxy; its error spans are the ingress/egress mirror of failed checkout requests, not errors generated by its own configuration.

Add a readinessProbe (and a startupProbe) against the payment gRPC endpoint on containerPort 8080 so the pod is only added to the Service endpoints once the gRPC server is actually listening, given that the process needs ~78s after container start (observed 05:36:17Z -> 05:37:34.791Z) and the container currently has no probe at all; consider also minReadySeconds / maxUnavailable=0 for rollouts of this single-replica Deployment.

Investigate why the payment process takes ~78s from container start to opening its gRPC port (likely a dependency wait, e.g. on flagd/otel-collector) and reduce or gate it, and review the RequestErrorRate alert threshold: it fires on any error rate above 0, which the cluster's steady background error level (0.0037-0.0118 errored spans/s on frontend-proxy outside the burst) can satisfy.

gaps: Jaeger returned no traces for frontend, frontend-proxy or checkout in the incident window (traces_search/traces_search_by_tags returned no_data for 05:30-05:59Z), so span-level error details, exact gRPC status codes on checkout's Charge client spans and any parent-child call edges could not be verified; span-metric counts are span counts, not unique request counts.

Prometheus returned no alerting or recording rules at all (list_prometheus_rules for rule_name RequestErrorRate and for type=alert both returned no_data), so the RequestErrorRate expression, its evaluation window/threshold and the reported value 0.01111111111111111 could not be verified.
The change-history integration is not available in this Run, so why the kubectl rollout restart (restartedAt 2026-11-15T05:36:13Z) was issued and who issued it are unknown.
Metric samples for these series end at about 05:51:00Z (instant query at 05:58:00Z returned no data), so frontend-proxy's error rate and whether the alert resolved after 05:51Z are unknown.

Checkout pod logs were truncated by the line limit before 05:38:27Z (227-346 earlier lines omitted), so the client-side error text for the first failures (05:36:18Z-05:38:27Z) was not read; a filtered query for error/fail/charge keywords over 05:34-05:42Z returned no matching lines (no_data) rather than showing an application-level error message.
The previous payment pod (payment-55766d76b9-5frt4) no longer exists, so its container logs and shutdown behaviour could not be inspected.
Only the payment pod template was inspected for probe presence; whether other otel-demo workloads also lack readiness/startup probes was not checked.
next_steps: Review the payment Deployment rollout that was triggered at 2026-11-15T05:36:13Z in the cluster's audit/change history (not integrated here) to identify the operator or pipeline behind it.
Add a readinessProbe/startupProbe on containerPort 8080 to the payment container and re-test a single-replica rollout to confirm no Charge failures occur.
Confirm the RequestErrorRate alert rule definition (expression, window, threshold) and whether a non-zero threshold with a for-duration would avoid firing on the steady background error level.
Check whether other otel-demo deployments with slow-starting applications (e.g. frontend, checkout) also lack readiness probes.
